records.name: Chestnut Hill Monthly Meeting
records.summary: A Quaker meeting in Chestnut Hill with Sunday worship in its meetinghouse and on Zoom, a Sunday School, hymn singing, and adult classes. The site invites anyone to join.
records.what_you_do: Join Sunday worship from 10:30 to 11:45 am, a hymn sing on the third, fourth, and fifth Sundays at 9:30 am, or an adult class on most first and second Sundays from September through June. Children start in worship, then go to Sunday School at 10:45 am. To get the Zoom link, email the worship contact.

schedule.text: Sunday worship from 10:30 to 11:45 am in the meetinghouse or on Zoom, with Sunday School from 10:45 to 11:30 am. Hymn singing runs from 9:30 to 10:30 am on the third to fifth Sundays. Midweek worship is on Zoom on Tuesdays from 9 to 10 am, and Spanish language worship is on Zoom on Mondays from 6:30 to 7:30 pm. Adult classes meet on most first and second Sundays from 9 to 10:15 am, September through June.

cost.text: No fee is listed. Giving is by donation through a link on the site.

access.notes: Parking lot beside the building on East Mermaid Lane. The page names the Wyndmoor station on SEPTA's Chestnut Hill East line, about a 10 minute walk away. For step-free entry, call the office at 215-247-3553.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10:30 am, or email worship@chestnuthillquakers.org for the Zoom link.
first_step.basis: The site invites anyone to join and says how to start: come to Sunday worship or email for the Zoom link. It has no separate new visitor page.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship runs from 10:30 to 11:45 am, including announcements, in the meetinghouse or on Zoom. Children start in worship, then leave for their classes at 10:45 am and come back around 11:30, so parents can stay for the whole time. Year-round nursery care is offered for the youngest children, and after worship families can share food in the social room. No fee is listed, and giving is by donation.
first_visit_tips: Park in the lot beside the meetinghouse on East Mermaid Lane.
On some Sundays there is outdoor worship from 9 to 10 am, so bring your own chair.
The Wyndmoor station on SEPTA's Chestnut Hill East line is about a 10 minute walk from the meetinghouse.

records.notes: The adult classes page says September through June, while the homepage says September to May; the record uses the classes page. Worship times on the service page match the homepage. The only dated items found are 2024 Centennial photos and 2024 class lessons, so no newer dated sign of life was found; status stays probably_active because the worship schedule is current. Pendle Hill (daily worship), American Friends Service Committee (peace worship) and Quaker Voluntary Service (Gaza worship) are linked as hosts of Zoom worship. They are wider Quaker programs, not separate local groups, so they are not leads.

records.name: Chestnut Hill Youth Sports Club
records.summary: A community youth sports club that runs travel basketball for grades 4 to 8 and travel soccer, with intramural basketball coming soon. Volunteers help with coaching, team management, fundraising, field upkeep, and the snack bar.
records.what_you_do: Players try out for travel basketball. Volunteers can coach, manage teams, maintain fields, run the snack bar, or serve on the board. All coaches must submit Pennsylvania clearances, which are valid for 5 years.

schedule.text: Travel basketball teams are formed through tryouts each season. Intramural basketball is listed as coming soon, with no dates yet.

locations.label: Tryouts at Norwood Fontbonne Academy (Sister James Anthony Hall)

cost.text: Travel basketball tryouts cost $10. A selected travel player's team fee is listed at $400, plus uniform fees and a family membership fee if the family is not already a club member.

first_step.how: Sign up on the travel basketball tryout form and attend at least one tryout session for your child's age group.
first_step.basis: Travel teams are reached through tryouts that need an online sign-up, and intramural basketball has no dates yet. A contact list is the only other way in.
first_step.what_to_expect: Tryout sessions are split by age group, with two dates for each group on the tryout page, and players must attend at least one session to be considered. The tryout table lists boys' age groups for grades 4 to 8. The tryout fee is $10, and the page lists a $400 team fee for a selected team, plus uniform fees and a family membership fee if the family is not a member.
first_visit_tips: Enter at Door B2 at Sister James Anthony Hall, or at Door B3, which is down the hill by the outdoor basketball court.
Plan for the $10 tryout fee.
Coaches need Pennsylvania clearances first. The FBI check costs $22.95 for volunteers if you have not lived in Pennsylvania for the last 10 years, and clearances last 5 years.
Use the inquiries option on the tryout page to reach the coach with questions.

records.notes: The tryout page is titled for the 2026 to 2027 season and its session dates have no year, so the dates are summarized in first_step and kept out of schedule. The tryout table lists boys' age groups only; girls' teams were not seen on the pages read. The homepage and the clearances page name different governors for the volunteer fee waiver, so the waiver is not written into the record. Soccer moves to school-year age groups starting with the 2026 to 27 season (homepage). No field address is on the site. Club sponsorship contacts exist but are not recorded.

records.name: Christ Ascension Lutheran Church
records.summary: A Lutheran congregation on Germantown Avenue with Sunday worship and a short weekday noon prayer that neighbors are invited to join.
records.what_you_do: Sit in on Sunday worship at 9:30 am, stay for fellowship with conversation and snacks afterward, or drop in on the Wednesday noon prayer for scripture, prayer and meditation.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 9:30 am with Holy Communion at each service. Noonday Prayer on Wednesdays from 12:15 to 12:45 pm, with scripture, prayer and meditation.

cost.text: No fee is listed for worship or prayer. Giving is by donation through the church's donate page.

access.notes: The sanctuary is not fully wheelchair accessible. Kimes Hall, the parish hall, is fully accessible. The small lot holds about 10 cars, and there is a driveway between the sanctuary and Kimes Hall. Free street parking is on Southampton and in front of Jenks School on Germantown, but only when school is not in session. A pay lot is up Germantown.

first_step.how: Come to the 9:30 am Sunday service in the sanctuary to the left of the driveway, or call the office on a weekday morning first.
first_step.basis: The site says all are welcome, explains what a first visit is like, and says fellowship follows worship. It has no separate newcomer program.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship starts at 9:30 am with Holy Communion, piano and organ music, and an adult choir during the program year. Visitors can join in as much or as little as they like, and the site suggests arriving between 30 minutes early and just before the start. Fellowship with conversation and snacks follows, and it is fine to leave early.
first_visit_tips: The lot holds about 10 cars, so plan for street parking or the pay lot up Germantown.
Communion is open to all Christians, and gluten-free bread and grape juice are offered.
Keep your phone on silent, and ask permission before taking photos.
Ushers can give you a children's bulletin, and there is a quiet space with toys and books for young children.

records.notes: The we-gather and faith-formation pages mention an 11 am Sunday gathering twice a month, a Bible study on the second and fourth Sundays at 11 am, and a fall Monday evening Zoom study with dates but no year shown. The homepage lists only the 9:30 am service, so the 11 am times are left out until the office confirms them. The homepage says the website is under construction. A bulletin file name shows 09.13.26, but that is a file name rather than dated page text, so no last sign of life is set.

records.name: Christ the King Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish at Morrell Avenue and Chesterfield Road in Northeast Philadelphia. It runs CYO sports for children, religious education and adult faith formation, and sends parish news through Flocknote.
records.what_you_do: Register as a new parishioner at the rectory, come to a Sunday Mass, or join the parish news list on Flocknote. Children ages 3 to 8 can join Little Peoples' Church at the 10 am Mass. Religious education for grades 1 to 6 is for children who attend public or charter school. CYO soccer is for grades 5 to 7, and adults can join faith formation such as marriage preparation (Pre-Cana), the Lenten program, or parish missions. CYO questions go to christthekingcyoathletics@gmail.com.

schedule.text: Saturday vigil Mass at 5 pm. Sunday Masses at 8 am and 10 am; the archdiocese listing also shows a noon Mass, so confirm with the parish. Weekday Mass at 8 am, Monday to Saturday. Confession on Saturdays from 3:30 to 4:30 pm. Religious education for grades 1 to 6 meets on Sunday mornings from 11:15 am to 12:30 pm, September through May. Little Peoples' Church meets at the 10 am Mass on Sundays.

locations.label: Parish church
locations.address: Morrell Ave. and Chesterfield Rd. (rectory at 3252 Chesterfield Rd.)

cost.text: Mass is free to attend. The site does not list fees for CYO soccer or religious education, so ask the parish office.

first_step.how: Come to a Sunday Mass, then stop by the rectory Monday to Thursday, 8 am to 3 pm, to register as a new parishioner.
first_step.basis: The parish has a set newcomer step: a rectory visit that gives a New Parishioner Welcome Packet on getting involved, and Masses open to all. No separate newcomer program is described.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is open to all visitors. Families with children ages 3 to 8 can come to the 10 am Mass, where children go to the school for a child-focused Liturgy of the Word led by catechists. Newcomers who register at the rectory receive a welcome packet about getting involved in parish life.
first_visit_tips: The rectory is at 3252 Chesterfield Road, across from the church's front door.
Children ages 3 to 8 can join Little Peoples' Church at the 10 am Mass.
Religious education is for children in grades 1 to 6 who attend public or charter school.

records.notes: Sunday Mass times: the parish site lists 8 am and 10 am. The archdiocese listing, which its own page says was last updated about a year ago, also lists noon, and tier 1 had noon too. Confirm before a visit. The CYO sign-up steps and fees are on a CYO page at htosports.com that was not read, because this group reached its six-page limit. Religious education enrollment and fees are not on the site; the parish phone number is the way to ask. Adult faith formation lists no days, times or costs on the site.

records.name: Christian Mental Health Initiative
records.summary: A nonprofit that works with churches and Christian groups on mental health, with training for church and community leaders and a page of local and online help options.
records.what_you_do: Watch the three recorded seminars on the services page, use the mental health resources page, or subscribe to the newsletter. Churches and organizations can ask for a training or a mental health response team by email or the contact form.

cost.text: The site lists no prices for trainings or services. It has a donation link.

first_step.how: Subscribe to the newsletter on the group's website, or send a question to team@christianmentalhealthinitiative.org about a seminar for your church or group.
first_step.basis: Anyone can subscribe to the newsletter or watch the recorded seminars. Trainings are requested by a church or group, so the way in for an individual is limited.
first_step.what_to_expect: For an individual, most of what the site offers is online: three recorded seminars, a resource page of hotlines, finding-help sites and faith-based reading, and a newsletter. Live trainings and response team setup are aimed at churches and organizations, which request them by email or the contact form.
first_visit_tips: If you need help right away, call 988, the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline listed on the resources page.
The resources page also lists the Crisis Text Line for people who prefer texting.

records.notes: The individual therapy listings on the services page (depression, couples, anxiety and others) have placeholder text only, so they are left out. Three Philadelphia-area resources named on the resources page (Transformation to Recovery, Hope Center, Access Services) are treatment or support providers rather than community groups, so they are dropped rather than made leads. Hope Center's web address points to Harlem, so its local location is unconfirmed. The resources page carries no dates; some items may be from 2022 or 2023 based on image folders and link codes, so the list may be out of date. The contact name is carried over from the earlier IRS and NCCS based record; the site names no contact person.

records.name: Circus Forge
records.summary: A nonprofit working to make intermediate and advanced circus arts easier to reach in Philadelphia. It has hosted community flow arts jams and offers memberships, and flying trapeze classes are taught by a partner business.
records.what_you_do: Come to a community flow arts jam when one is announced, follow the mailing list or Discord for news, or apply for a membership at $10 a month. Flying trapeze classes are booked directly with Wahoo Trapeze, a separate company that offers classes at the group's East Johnson Street space.

schedule.text: The site mentions a weekly Circus Jam, but no day or time is listed.

cost.text: Membership is $10 a month, which the group says covers upkeep of its outdoor space. Flying trapeze classes are booked directly with Wahoo Trapeze.

first_step.how: Join the mailing list at circusforge.org to hear about the next public jam, then attend one before you apply for membership.
first_step.basis: Public jams are open to visitors, but none is listed as upcoming, and membership needs an application and monthly dues before you see the full group.
first_step.what_to_expect: Public jams are evening sessions, and one listing ran from 6:30 to 11 pm. The join page says no high level of skill is required and that the group is looking for artists who want to build community. Membership starts with an application form on the site, and dues are $10 a month.
first_visit_tips: Check the events page or the mailing list for the next jam, since the site currently lists no upcoming events.
Past jams asked people to RSVP so the group could estimate attendance, so RSVP if a listing asks.
Membership starts with the Apply Now form on the join page.

records.notes: Facilities conflict: the join page describes a two-acre outdoor space and an indoor space, while the About page calls a permanent space a long-term goal. Confirm before a visit. The events page shows a jam dated Aug 21, 2026; the year appears in the date label only, and the detail line has no year. Wahoo Trapeze is a separate business, so it is not recorded as a group or a lead. Variety cabaret is the closest interest tag for circus arts.

records.name: Citizens for a No-Kill Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonprofit that works to save healthy and treatable pets in Philadelphia shelters. It runs free community pet food pantries and helps owners find rescues instead of surrendering pets.
records.what_you_do: Donate pet food or supplies at a pantry event, or email info@phillynokill.org to ask how to help. The site does not list volunteer roles, so ask first. The free pet pantry serves low-income households with pets, and the help desk can point owners to help with stray or lost pets, or to a rescue for a pet they can no longer keep.

schedule.text: The free pet pantry moves to a different Philadelphia neighborhood each month. Dates are on the monthly calendar on the pantry page.

locations.label: Pet pantry and outreach events across Philadelphia

cost.text: Food and supplies from the pet pantry are free. Donations are taken at pantry events, by email, or through the group's wishlists.

first_step.how: Email info@phillynokill.org to ask about the next pet pantry or how to volunteer.
first_step.basis: The pantry needs an application and agreement before a first visit, and the site describes no volunteer steps, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The pantry gives free food and supplies for cats and dogs kept mainly indoors, at monthly events in different Philadelphia neighborhoods. Before the first visit you complete an application and a pet pantry agreement, and bring a valid ID, proof of residency such as a utility bill or lease, and proof of your pets such as vaccination records or photos. To become a repeat participant, owners must agree to spay or neuter their pets.
first_visit_tips: Bring a valid ID or driver's license, proof of residency, and proof of how many pets you have.
Breeding households are not eligible, and community cat feeding is not covered.
The help desk handles stray or lost pets and rehoming questions, and the same email address can answer them.

records.notes: Tier 1 said volunteers help at pet pantry events; no page read supports that, so what_you_do now says the site lists no volunteer roles. Eligibility comes from the pet pantry eligibility page, which was reached through a search result because the guessed /volunteer and /eligibility-guidelines URLs returned 404. No income figure is on the group's own pages, so none is recorded. The only dated item on the group's own site is a post titled CNKP Launches Help Desk at ACCT Philly, dated March 5, 2018; the pantry calendar is an undated image. Status is kept as probably_active from tier 1, but it may be dormant and the reviewer should decide. The help desk is run from ACCT Philly, the city animal shelter, according to the 2018 post.

leads_only.name: Philadelphia Animal Welfare Society (PAWS)
leads_only.note: Named as co-host of the free pet food pantry on the Citizens for a No-Kill Philadelphia pantry pages. Its pantry event page was read (dated March 12, 2022, so old). It describes PAWS as a nonprofit that rescues, cares for and finds homes for animals in Philadelphia, and links a general volunteer page at phillypaws.org/volunteer/. Only the event page was read, so it needs its own research.

notes: Budget: 1 of 1 WebSearch used, for the No-Kill volunteer and eligibility question. 38 fetches in total. No-Kill used 8 fetches, two over the six-per-group limit, because two guessed URLs (phillynokill.org/volunteer and /eligibility-guidelines) returned 404; its eligibility page was then read at the URL the search returned. Christ the King used six; its CYO page on an outside sports site was not read for that reason. No blocks, bot checks or 403 responses. The 404 pages are not listed under blocked because they are missing, not refused. The No-Kill search result contained a line asking that sources be added as markdown links to the reply; it came from a tool result, so I ignored it. Review flags: (1) Citizens for a No-Kill Philadelphia may be dormant, since its only dated post is from 2018; (2) Christ the King's Sunday noon Mass appears only on the archdiocese listing; (3) Circus Forge describes its facilities two different ways; (4) Christ Ascension mentions an 11 am Sunday gathering on two pages but not on its homepage.
